Option-letter next-token probabilities with the package calibration temperatures. readout.portable_notes: The unmodified author library/CLI accepts CPU or MPS and keeps BF16 in its LLM loader: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ncchinh/quyet/f9bddb97bf0e39c8c965a85c0c6c5d1295224b6a/src/quyet/cli.py L18: p.add_argument("--device", help="cpu, cuda, cuda:1, ... (default: cuda if available)"); L21: model = load(a.model, device=a.device). https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ncchinh/quyet/f9bddb97bf0e39c8c965a85c0c6c5d1295224b6a/src/quyet/llm/runtime.py L22: dtype = dtype or torch.bfloat16; L29: model = model.to(device). 31B CPU execution is technically selectable but not practical; no CPU installer variant is offered. BF16 62.546 GB +25% =78.18 GB (~72.8 GiB), so a 64 GB Mac cannot fit; only a 96 GB+ Mac candidate is added, unbenchmarked. Readout is in-process and requires its calibrated label probabilities; backend_agnostic=false.

steps: Pull the pinned image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0@sha256:8a69ffad... (only for its python 3.12.3 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 / transformers 5.17.0 runtime).
Fetch chinhnc/Quyet-1.0-Large at e1ecbbe7; verify MANIFEST.sha256 and pinned shard sha256 7e06d4a9... and f06a5e11....
Put quyet src (github.com/ncchinh/quyet @ f9bddb9) on sys.path; run quyet_local.QuyetLocalAdapter with model_dir=<snapshot>, device=cuda, dtype bf16.
Run with --network none, --read-only, --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges (BH hardening).
